title: Strict completion of point pairings and normalization of the tensor comparison
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum with $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ and $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$, and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $R=\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. On the small pro-etale site $s_{\mathrm{proet}}$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], put $A_m=(R/\varpi^m)_s$ for $m\ge1$ and $B=\varprojlim_m A_m$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. For an $R$-module $M$ let $\underline M$ be its constant sheaf [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf] and put $L(M)=B\otimes_{\underline R}\underline M$, using sheaf tensor [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]; apply $L$ and $\Gamma=\Gamma(s,-)$ termwise to complexes.
Let $P$ be a bounded finite-projective $R$-module complex [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex], put $C=L(P)$, and let $J$ be a bounded complex of flat $B$-modules [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]. Put $D=\operatorname{Tot}(C\otimes_BJ)$ with signed total tensor [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. Assume the terms of $C$ are flat, the actual unit $P\to\Gamma C$, $x\mapsto1\otimes x$, is a quasi-isomorphism, $\Gamma B=R$ by constant values, and $B[0],C,J,D$ belong to $D^b_c(s,R)$, with $C,J$ of finite Tor amplitude [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed, def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]. For any chain map $e:D\to B[0]$, let $e_m:D\otimes_B A_m\to A_m[0]$ be its reduction. Write $H$ for the specified functorial shifted cone $\operatorname{Cone}(1-t:\prod_m(-)_m\to\prod_m(-)_m)[-1]$ on strict quotient towers [def-weil-strict-roos-model]. Use completed tensor and completed pairing $\widehat e:C\widehat\otimes_R^LJ\to B$ from the integral tensor/internal-Hom adjunction [def-pur-integral-derived-operations, def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom].
The balancing isomorphisms $D\otimes_B A_m\cong(C\otimes_B A_m)\otimes_{A_m}(J\otimes_B A_m)$, $(c\otimes j)\otimes a\mapsto(c\otimes1)\otimes(j\otimes a)$, form an isomorphism of strict towers and identify $H(D\otimes_B A_m)$ with $C\widehat\otimes_R^LJ$. The specified identity-extension maps [lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison] give isomorphisms $\chi_D:D\xrightarrow{\sim}C\widehat\otimes_R^LJ$ and $\chi_B:B\xrightarrow{\sim}H(A_m)$, with quotient-map product coordinate and zero shifted-product coordinate. The reduction squares of $e$ commute strictly, and their induced cone map satisfies $H(e_m)\chi_D=\chi_B e$ before localization. The canonical completed pairing is $\widehat e=\chi_B^{-1}H(e_m)$, and hence $\widehat e\chi_D=e$ in the derived category.
Let $\beta:P\otimes_R^L\Gamma J\to\Gamma D$ be sections balancing, induced on generators by $x\otimes h\mapsto(1\otimes x)\otimes h$. The canonical point tensor comparison $\tau:\Gamma(C\widehat\otimes_R^LJ)\xrightarrow{\sim}P\otimes_R^L\Gamma J$ [lem-sf-point-fibre-derived-tensor], using the displayed unit to identify $\Gamma C$ with $P$, satisfies $\tau^{-1}=\Gamma(\chi_D)\beta$. This normalization uses those same quotient coordinates, including the zero shifted-product coordinate.

proof.text: The bounded-above flat criterion gives good representatives C and J. Apply the K-flat total tensor model to get the same for Tot(C,J); B[0] is the tensor unit and has flat terms. The balanced quotient tower lemma gives rho with its formula on every local generator.

The normalized completed-line unitor theorem and its intrinsic completeness conversion imply that the actual localized identity-extension unit is a composite of isomorphisms. Apply this to the total and B[0]. The unit defining existence-and-uniqueness theorem gives both quotient-product and zero shifted coordinates. Naturality of the scalar reduction on local generators proves each quotient square; naturality of the specified unit proves the chain square.

The definition of chi is the localized total unit composed with two isomorphisms, so chi is invertible. Define b to be the isomorphism of the localized coefficient unit. Expand completedPairing, cancel the representative and rho isomorphisms, and apply the chain naturality square. Cancellation with b gives chi followed by completedPairing equal to Q(e). Since chi is an isomorphism, precomposition with it is injective and supplies the unique pairing. The complete-total hypothesis makes a separate reflector Hom-bijection unnecessary here.

Apply the chain-level sections balancing completion lemma to eta and the balanced rho. Its generator formula supplies beta and its chain square is precisely betaCompletionEquation. Localize that square. Naturality of pointIntegralDerivedFactors, naturality of the module localization tensorator, and the comparison field of the given canonical witness identify its two sides with the requested inverseTensorComparison equation. The inverse/hom equations for the same factors cancel the transport maps.
